name: Zebadiah
overview: Zebadiah was a male figure identified as the son of Jeroham from Gedor. He is noted for coming to David at Ziklag, indicating his allegiance during a significant period in Israel's history. His tribal affiliation is not recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Zebadiah means 'YHWH bestows,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to the Lord's providence. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:7 and was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Zebadiah as the son of Jeroham, as noted in 1 Chronicles 12:7. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family ties are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Zebadiah's significance lies in his support of David during a pivotal moment, as he came to David at Ziklag. This act illustrates his loyalty and contributes to the narrative of David's consolidation of support among Israel's warriors. His identification as the son of Jeroham of Gedor places him within the community that aligned with David's kingship.
